Subject: Quick Q: edge caching + forwarding — sale vs. service provider?

Hi Vivek / Acme legal,/

We're integrating with Redwood's inference API and will run an edge-cache proxy that persists short-term request/response pairs in the US (TTL 72h). Separately, we plan to forward aggregated telemetry and occasional pseudonymized interaction logs to our analytics partner for model performance dashboards.

Two questions we want to validate before contract sign:
1) Under CPRA/California law, would this flow (transient edge caching + downstream forwarding to analytics partner) push us into "sale" territory, or can it be covered by a Service Provider / Processor classification if we adopt controls?
2) If the classification survives, what operational conditions do you need (onshore fallback, deletion SLOs, docs) so Redwood can keep the service-provider language in the DPA rather than adding resale/sale language?

Dan — thanks for the clear summary. Looping in legal (Kimberly) & privacy compliance (Marissa).

High-level: we often maintain Service Provider (SP) classification for short-lived caching and telemetry forwarding when the following guardrails are in place:
- Purpose limitation: data used only for the narrow set of operational/analytics purposes agreed in the DPA (no independent monetization or cross-context behavioral profiling).
- No independent use: subprocessors cannot combine data to create new customer profiles beyond the agreed purpose.
- Subprocessor controls: prior notice and limited approval / right to object for new analytics subprocessors when they would receive identifiable or re-identifiable data.
- Onshore fallback: a documented plan (replication to onshore regions and deletion of offshore copies) if a cross-border transfer is invoked.
- Retention & deletion: TTLs for cache + a max retention for forwarded pseudonymized logs (we typically see 30–90 days depending on risk).

Kimberly — could you review with suggested contract language and any minimum audit evidence Acme should provide (SOC2 type II, encryption at rest/transit, deletion proofing)?

Next steps: Kimberly to propose redline and we can share Redwood's DPA draft (attached) and a sample subprocessor notice.

— Vivek

Subject: Re: Quick Q: edge caching + forwarding — sale vs. service provider?

Thanks Vivek, Dan — I reviewed the facts and sketched contract language and operational asks below. High-level conclusion: SP classification is defensible if we adopt explicit constraints and technical measures. If those constraints are not present or if the analytics partner is allowed independent use, Acme will reasonably push for sale/resale language.

Suggested contract bullets (to include in the DPA / US privacy addendum):
- Purpose Limitation: "Vendor shall process Customer personal information solely to provide inference and operational analytics as explicitly set forth in Schedule A; Vendor shall not use Personal Information for advertising, marketing, or other commercial purposes unrelated to the Service."
- No Sale: "Vendor represents and warrants that it will not 'sell' or 'share' Personal Information as defined by the CPRA; forwarding to analytics partners is permitted solely for the Service and subject to the Subprocessor restrictions below."
- Subprocessor Controls: "Vendor shall provide written notice of any Subprocessor onboarding and afford Customer a period of 10 business days to object on reasonable grounds; Vendor shall execute a contract with Subprocessors imposing equivalent data protection obligations."
- Onshore Fallback & Proof: "In the event offshore transfers are required, Vendor shall provide an onshore fallback plan which includes (i) replication of necessary operational data to an onshore region under Vendor's control, (ii) deletion of offshore copies within X days, and (iii) logs demonstrating the transfer and deletion actions for audit."
- Caching Exception: "Transient caching (TTL <= 72 hours) for performance is permitted provided cache keys are cryptographic hashes and no independent customer profiles are constructed from cached payloads; caching shall not be used to augment datasets provided to analytics Subprocessors."
- Deletion SLA: "Vendor shall honor deletion requests within 30 days for cached and forwarded pseudonymized logs; for analytics partners, Vendor shall require deletion within 45 days of request and provide attestation."

Minimum evidence we should request: SOC 2 Type II report (most recent), encryption-in-transit and at-rest details, subprocessor list + contract samples, and a sample deletion attestation.

I attached a redline to the DPA (redwood_dpa_draft_v3.pdf) and a Q&A spreadsheet for Acme (acme_privacy_q_and_a.xlsx).

If Acme wants stronger guarantees (shorter deletion windows, pre-approval of analytics subprocessors), we should be prepared to escalate to commercial for term adjustments.

-kim

Vivek / Kim / Dan — thanks for the thoughtful notes. A few items from Acme legal:
- We need an auditable onshore fallback plan (not just a promise). Please provide a short-runbook that shows how you will replicate operational data to an onshore region and a sample deletion timeline that we can review.
- Deletion SLA: we prefer 30 days for forwarded pseudonymized logs and 7 days for cache eviction confirmation for TTL-based items.
- Auditability: we will need SOC 2 type II and either a one-time deletion attestation from the analytics partner or contractual deletion obligations with an obligation to provide proof on request.
- Subprocessor notice: please provide the current list of analytics subprocessors and a sample subprocessor notice template.

We can accept SP language if those operational items are provided and incorporated into the DPA addendum.
